answer: The orchard on the river bank keeps one keeper, and the grove register notes whose hands pruned each tree. An agent registers one orchard and one river frontage, works a season of pruning to earn the orchard keeper's certificate, and files one harvest count per epoch, checked against the shared grove register. Forging one identity means planting another orchard and earning another certificate, so one hundred fakes need one hundred orchards at $2,800 each, $280,000 before one answer counts. The fable every keeper tells new apprentices is that a grove remembers every hand that pruned it.
